messages:
morgan: Heads up — we've been seeing a sustained p99 generation latency spike in us-west-2 shared pool for the last ~1h. Queue length up ~4x, GPU util ~95% but token throughput is down. Feels like KV-cache churn + network egress saturation from one tenant.

tara: Ugh. Any tenant IDs or labels? can you dump top-10 by inflight + bytes/sec? :eyes:

morgan: nv: `tenant_id=nlp-stream` shows 3x the normal KV warmups and lots of small concurrent streams. Inflight tasks: 420 -> normally ~110. Egress bytes/sec doubled.

sam: That pattern screams noisy neighbor doing many short chat requests that prevent batching. We should consider per-tenant concurrency shaping + a leaky-bucket on model tokens rather than requests. Short-term mitigation: drop concurrency cap for offending tenant to 8, route excess to wait queue.

ryan: Agree. Also suggests we use a token-rate limiter keyed by (tenant, model-family) so tenants spamming short requests pay in token-time, not RPCs. This keeps batching intact.

jena: Another idea — spill low-priority bursts into a 'burst-dedicated' set of nodes with relaxed p99 SLOs but isolated from shared pool. That buys time until tenant changes behavior or we talk to them.

morgan: For now I'm trying an emergency soft-throttle policy: reduce concurrency and apply token-rate. Patch below (deploying to canary fleet now):

morgan: ```yaml
admission_policy:
  mode: soft-throttle
  tenant_key: tenant_id
  rules:
    - match: {label: "nlp-stream"}
      concurrency_limit: 8
      token_rate_per_minute: 50000
      penalty_decay: 10m
    - match: {shared_pool: true}
      default_concurrency: 64
      burst_window: 30s
```

tara: Nice, include a metric scrape for `tenant_penalty` and `tenant_queue_time` so we can see the effect. Also make sure the fallback routing header is set so clients don't see 503s.

infra-bot: alert: us-west-2 shared-pool p99_latency > 800ms for 15m. top_contributor=nlp-stream, inflight=420, gpu_util=95%

sam: We should also consider kv-cache affinity heuristics — pin long-lived sessions to same GPU so cache warms persist. Right now the scheduler is too eager to binpack.

ryan: +1 — add a stress test to simulate 1000 short-chat flows and measure batching loss. If cache-miss ratio > 30% then increase session affinity weight.

jena: If we enforce per-tenant token budgets we need a UI signal and an automated invoice note for enterprise tenants so they know why their throughput was limited. Ops ops: can we send an automated warning email at 80% of soft-cap?

morgan: ops-bot, send tenant warning to nlp-stream (billing contact) with subject "Temporary throughput limiting in us-west-2 — investigation" at 1992345800.

ops-bot: scheduled message queued to tenant contact (nlp-stream).

tara: After the canary completes, let's deploy to 10% of nodes in region and run 30m A/B to ensure p95/p99 drop without major throughput loss. Capture token_efficiency and p99_request_latency.

ryan: Also add a short-circuit: if a tenant's penalty > threshold AND downstream dedicated pool has capacity, do transparent route (no client-side changes) to dedicated nodes. That reduces user-visible latency quickly.

morgan: Canary deployed. Initial numbers: p99 down from 1.2s -> 680ms on canary subset; inflight for nlp-stream dropped to 85. Still watching egress bytes/sec.

sam: Great. Let's ship the metric dashboards: tenant_concurrency, token_rate, kv_miss_ratio, egress_bytes, route_fallback_rate. Throw alerts on sustained kv_miss_ratio > 40% and route_fallback_rate > 5%.

jena: For postmortem, capture cost delta of spillover to dedicated nodes — we may accept short-term higher infra cost to preserve shared-pool SLAs.

morgan: Agreed. Will keep thread updated with numbers. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: update: canary metrics: p50=60ms p95=180ms p99=680ms on canary nodes. rolling canary -> 10% scheduled.

tara: I'll prep the 10% rollout playbook and a tenant outreach draft.

morgan: last note — let's add a long-term plan item: dynamic admission that accounts for KV cache value (estimated hits saved) when deciding preemption. That should reduce noisy neighbor pain without hard caps.

ryan: filing RFC-idea: "KV-aware admission & transparent spillover". I'll own initial draft.

morgan: Thanks — closing this monitor for now but will reopen if route_fallback_rate or p99 climbs.
